title: auth-api 401/429 debug scratchpad - jordan
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad while investigating recurring 401/429s reported by a customer (org: acme-corp). Notes are messy - timeline, commands tried, snippets from logs, and hypotheses. Will extract formal postmortem if this escalates.

Summary of problem seen: 
- Customer hitting intermittent 401 Unauthorized and 429 Too Many Requests from hosted API endpoints. 401s show up primarily from mobile clients; 429s from server-to-server bulk ingestion jobs.
- 401s appear in bursts when the client resumes after a network flake. 429s spike when ingestion job increases concurrency after autoscale.

High-level hypothesis list (prioritized):
1) Client-side API key rotation / caching bug: token or key cached incorrectly and then rejected by auth service (401).
2) Token expiry / clock skew causing immediate 401 for short-lived tokens.
3) Edge rate-limiter mis-classifies legitimate traffic as abusive when requests arrive in concentrated bursts (429). 
4) Request routing to a misconfigured gateway node with stale quota counters (429).
5) Per-customer quota enforcement bug (wrongly using global bucket).

Commands / checks run so far:
1) Reproduced a 401 from my laptop: curl against hosted API with customer's API key (redacted).
   curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=rwkv-mini
   Response headers: 
     HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
     Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 14:12:09 GMT
     Content-Type: application/json
   Response body:
     {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found"}

2) Verified key exists in auth DB (kv-store):
   redis> GET api_key:acme-mobile-01
   -> "active:2026-06-01:scopes:generate"  (entry exists, TTL looks normal)

3) Hit auth service locally with a trace id and compared logs (auth-logs):
   TRACE-ID: trace-20260316-14-12-jk
   auth-service log: "key lookup success" -> forwarded to gateway -> gateway returned 401 with message from edge: "signature mismatch"
   Edge gateway log for same trace: "JWT signature verification failed: kid not found"
   - suspicious: customer's client is sometimes sending a signed JWT with kid header. We expect bearer keys for this integration.

4) Mobile client reproduction steps (adb logs):
   - App used cached JWT for quick resume after network loss (token generated by intermediate proxy). When proxy restarted, it began issuing JWTs signed with a new key id that is not present in edge's JWKS cache, so edge rejects (401).

5) 429 reproduction from ingestion job: used locust-style script to mimic ingestion concurrency
   - script: python stress_ingest.py --concurrency 120 --qps 600 --api-key ACME_INGEST_KEY
   Observed: immediate 429s with response body: {"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":2}
   - Some responses include Retry-After header, some don't. Inconsistent.

6) Checked gateway metrics around quota counters (datadog query):
   - For acme-corp, per-route counters spike then are reset by a background job that runs every 10s (bucket refill?). There are occasional negative deltas in counters recorded by the exporter (maybe wrap-around or race).

7) Pulled logs from region-a gateway node (node-37) that handled many 429s:
   node-37 log excerpt:
     2026-03-16T14:40:12Z [WARN] rate_limiter: allow=false key=acct:acme-corp route=/v1/embeddings qps=600 limit=500 window=1s
     2026-03-16T14:40:12Z [INFO] quota-sync: last_sync=2026-03-16T14:40:05Z status=ok
     2026-03-16T14:40:20Z [WARN] rate_limiter: allow=false key=acct:acme-corp route=/v1/embeddings qps=620 limit=500 window=1s
   Observations: limit looks like 500/s but exporter shows 450/s in product config. Mismatch between config store and runtime.

Quick checks against config store:
- curl to config-service: GET /accounts/acme-corp/quota -> returns {"per_second":500,"per_minute":30000}
- ui (console) shows 450/s -> caching tier might be stale.

Hypotheses refined after logs:
- 401s: caused by intermediate proxy issuing JWTs (with kid) that edge doesn't accept. Fix paths: detect bearer tokens that are actually JWTs and reject gracefully with clearer message; update JWKS cache refresh strategy; or remove JWT signing at proxy.
- 429s: mis-sync between config-service and gateway nodes -> gateway using 500/s limit while console and other nodes show 450/s. Could be due to async config propagation + exporter reporting weird deltas. Race when autoscaling causes many nodes to pick up stale config at once -> cumulative effective limit exceeded.

Next immediate mitigation steps (short-term):
- For 401s:
  - Add a temporary compatibility check in edge to accept old kid if fingerprint matches known keys OR return a clearer error to client suggesting key rotation/refresh.
  - Reach out to customer's mobile eng to check proxy restart patterns and JWT issuance.

- For 429s:
  - Throttle inbound concurrency at ingress LB for acme-corp to smooth bursts (set soft limit 420/s) for 48h while we investigate.
  - Force immediate config refresh on all gateway nodes (rolling restart if needed) to ensure consistent limits.

Longer term fixes to evaluate:
- Improve JWKS caching: subscribe to key-store change feed so edge receives key rotations within ~1s.
- Add per-node config version stamp; fail-fast if node config version older than n seconds for critical quota fields.
- Add canary rollout for config updates and better instrumentation for exporter deltas to detect wrap-around or negative counters.
- Make rate-limiter use consistent global token-bucket algorithm across nodes (centralized shepherd or strongly consistent counters for critical accounts).

Notes about experiments to run (TODOs):
- Run a controlled canary: push quota-change to test account, spin up 10 nodes, simulate autoscale, watch for discrepancies.
- Add unit tests for JWT/kid handling in edge auth codepath.
- Add integration test that simulates proxy restart and token caching semantics to reproduce 401 flow.

Random breadcrumbs:
- Found a slack thread: #cs-acme -> message id 16233 with customer timeline (12:30-14:50)
- Customer reported 401s coincide with push notification bursts from mobile devices (makes sense if proxy restarts around the same time).

Immediate messages I sent:
- Pinged Aisha (CS) asking for exact timestamps of incidents from customer logs.
- DM to Michael to schedule a rolling config refresh on region-a nodes.

Open questions / things I don't know yet:
- Why some 429 responses lack Retry-After header. Could be two different rate-limiter codepaths returning different shapes (legacy vs new).
- Whether exporter negative deltas are telemetry bug or actual counter resets. Need to check raw prometheus counters and collection intervals.
- If the auth proxy is intentionally signing tokens (it probably shouldn't). Need to confirm design doc for acme mobile integration.

Useful links / artifacts to attach later:
- auth-service logs query: logs://auth-service?trace=trace-20260316-14-12-jk
- gateway node logs: s3://gateway-logs/region-a/node-37/2026-03-16.log
- datadog dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/abc123/rate-limiter-explorer

TODO (ordered):
- [ ] Get precise customer timestamps from CS (Aisha)
- [ ] Force config refresh on region-a nodes (Michael)
- [ ] Add temporary ingress soft-throttle for acme-corp
- [ ] Reproduce 401 locally with proxy restart + cached JWT flow and capture full headers
- [ ] Add unit/integration test for kid/JWKS mismatch path

If this becomes a Sev, extract timeline and make an incident postmortem with root cause and action items. For now keep as working notes.

-- Jordan
